3.4.1.4-f1.accuracy_reason: The gloss of 'ad vitam corrigi' as reform of their way of life is questionable. Set against burning, it more likely means to be corrected and so keep their lives.

3.4.1.4-f12.accuracy_reason: In Juvenal 6.525–527 the woman crawls on bleeding knees, and 'si candida iusserit Io' begins the next clause about going to Egypt, so Burton does join the two.

3.4.1.4-f6.accuracy_reason: De beneficiis 4.5.1 reads 'non necessitatibus tantum nostris provisum est: usque in delicias amamur'. The doubt about which quotation the sidenote belongs to is properly hedged.
